coordinate_convention: Planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude in -180..180, IAU2000 Mars reference (same convention as MOLA MEGDR). Positions are rover/lander touchdown points or the published centre of a selected landing ellipse.
footprint_definition: Square footprint of half-width 0.5 degrees (about 59 km N-S, 59*cos(lat) km E-W) centred on the site coordinates. Chosen to hold 17x17 MOLA MEGDR 16 ppd cells (floor/ceil edges) so slope and roughness statistics are populated; it is a REGIONAL footprint, far larger than any landing ellipse. Positions are rover/lander touchdown points or the published centre of a selected landing ellipse where the app already held one within ~20 km of the workbook's point; otherwise the coordinates compiled in the Lesser-Known Mars Sites workbook (some flagged approximate).

sites.name: Amazonis / Arcadia Planitia (AP-8)
sites.description: Candidate landing site AP-8 on the boundary between Arcadia and northern Amazonis Planitia, in the northern mid-latitudes; mapped thermal contraction polygons point to ice tens of centimetres below the surface.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Near-surface excess ice: ice beneath the mapped polygons is estimated at tens of cm depth (Luzzi et al., 2025).

sites.name: North Pole (Planum Boreum)
sites.description: The north polar ice cap: about 2 km of layered ice, sand and dust (the north polar layered deposits) above an ice-sand basal unit, estimated at about 4 million years old.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Massive water ice: radar shows thick ice-and-dust layers separated by layers of nearly pure ice (NASA PIA10652).

sites.name: South Pole (Planum Australe)
sites.description: The south polar cap: a water ice-rich polar cap with a permanent carbon dioxide ice cap; the Mars Polar Lander site lies about 2.4 km high, midway into the polar layered terrain.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Water ice-rich south polar cap (NASA PIA26773).

sites.name: Mawrth Vallis
sites.description: Ancient channel on the dichotomy boundary with a 25 km impact crater; thick light-toned clays rich in iron, magnesium and aluminium, up to about 200 m deep, under dark volcanic caps.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Liquid water ran through Mawrth Vallis about 3.6 billion years ago (ESA Mars Express); no modern ice reported in the cited sources.

sites.name: Noctis Labyrinthus
sites.description: Maze of troughs and pits at the western end of Valles Marineris; many of its depressions contain water-bearing minerals.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Water-bearing minerals in many depressions, suggesting water was available during the Late Hesperian to Amazonian (NASA PIA18632).

sites.name: Hebrus Valles
sites.description: Channel system in the northern lowlands west of the Elysium volcanic region, with deep pits that may be cave entrances in carbonate- and sulfate-rich rock.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Pits might retain subsurface water ice (HiRISE ESP_048036_2025); GRS data show elevated water-equivalent hydrogen (Sharma et al., 2025).

sites.name: Huygens Crater
sites.region: Noachian highlands near the Hellas rim
sites.description: Large double-ring impact crater, about 470 km across, in the heavily cratered southern highlands.

sites.name: Columbus Crater
sites.description: Crater in Terra Sirenum that likely hosted a lake: sulfate deposits overlie clays and ring the crater like a bathtub ring.
sites.water_ice_evidence: A past lake; sulfates were deposited after the clays as the lake dried out (NASA). No modern ice reported in the cited sources.

sites.name: Oxia Planum
sites.region: Chryse Planitia margin / Mawrth Vallis region
sites.heritage: ESA ExoMars Rosalind Franklin rover selected landing site
sites.description: Low-relief terrain of hydrous clay-bearing bedrock with a later fluviodeltaic system. ESA's selected landing site for the Rosalind Franklin rover.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Hydrous clay-bearing bedrock from past aqueous activity (Quantin-Nataf et al., 2021); no ice reported in the cited sources.

sites.name: Deuteronilus Mensae
sites.description: Fretted terrain on the dichotomy boundary: mesas surrounded by lobate debris aprons that radar shows to be nearly pure ice.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Lobate debris aprons composed of nearly pure ice (SHARAD radar, NASA PIA12996).

sites.name: Protonilus Mensae
sites.description: Fretted terrain on the dichotomy boundary with gully debris-flow deposits and a long record of possible periglacial and glacial cycling.

sites.name: Chryse Planitia (Viking 1)
sites.description: Northern plains near the terminus of the Maja Valles flood channel; Viking 1 imaged a boulder-strewn surface here.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Catastrophic flood and possible megatsunami deposits (Rodriguez et al., 2022); no ice reported in the cited sources.
sites.notes: Not probable as base; good area data

sites.name: Meridiani Planum
sites.description: Plains with extensive layered deposits, some rich in hematite, spanning units from the Early Noachian to the Late Amazonian; water-altered bedrock outcrops record past fluid-rock interaction.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Water-altered bedrock outcrops record prolonged surface and near-surface fluid/rock interaction (Hynek & Di Achille, 2017); no ice reported in the cited sources.
sites.notes: Narrowed to NASA human exploration-zone point

sites.name: Jezero Crater
sites.description: Impact crater whose floor holds water-altered igneous rocks below a sedimentary delta; its fan deposits carry Mg-rich carbonate, olivine and Fe/Mg-smectite. Perseverance landing site.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Ancient lake and river deposits (Farley et al., 2022); no ice reported in the cited sources.
sites.notes: Not a base; good for instrument-test matches

sites.name: Utopia Planitia (Zhurong area)
sites.heritage: Near the CNSA Tianwen-1 Zhurong rover landing region (2021)
sites.description: Southern Utopia Planitia near the Zhurong rover landing region, where manganese (hydr)oxides are interpreted as a record of a Hesperian ocean.

sites.name: Elysium Planitia (InSight)
sites.description: Smooth plains of impact-fragmented regolith over basaltic lava flows. InSight landing site.
sites.water_ice_evidence: No ice reported in the cited sources.

sites.name: Xanthe Terra (Tyras Vallis delta)
sites.notes: Not a base; match with Earth sites for testing
sites.description: Highland valleys of Xanthe Terra with fan-shaped deltaic deposits at the mouth of Tyras Vallis.
